name: Binance
look: Binance Yellow doing all the brand voltage on a flat dark canvas, with a deliberately light footer closing the page.

hero.title: Trade on the deepest books
hero.sub: Six hundred pairs, sub-millisecond matching, and a fee schedule that drops as your volume rises. Published maker rebates from the first tier.

features.title: Built for people who watch the spread
features.sub: Depth, latency and fees — the three numbers an active trader checks before funding anything.

items.title: Deep order books
items.body: Six hundred pairs with market-maker programmes keeping spreads tight through volatility.

items.title: Sub-millisecond matching
items.body: A matching engine measured in microseconds, with latency published per region.

items.title: Maker rebates
items.body: Negative maker fees from the first VIP tier rather than the fifth, published in full.

items.title: Proof of reserves
items.body: Merkle-tree attestations published quarterly with a self-verification tool.

items.title: Trading API
items.body: REST and WebSocket with documented rate limits and a testnet mirroring production.

items.title: Cold storage
items.body: Ninety-five percent held offline across geographically separated vaults.

showcases.title: Funding rates you can read
showcases.body: Perpetual funding, mark price and the index composition are all published, updated live. When a position gets liquidated you can see exactly which inputs produced it rather than filing a support ticket.

showcases.title: The mechanism, before the number
showcases.body: Every earn product states where the yield comes from, the counterparty, the lock-up and what happens under stress — on the product page, before you opt in.
points: Source of yield stated per product

gallery.title: MARKETS
gallery.sub: Spot, margin and perpetual futures across six hundred pairs.

testimonial.quote: The funding-rate page tells you the index composition. I have used four exchanges and this is the only one where a liquidation was explainable afterwards.
testimonial.name: Marco Ferretti

pricing.title: FEES
pricing.sub: Thirteen VIP tiers by 30-day volume. All published.

items.q: How is proof of reserves verified?
items.a: Balances are hashed into a Merkle tree audited quarterly against on-chain holdings, with a tool that lets you confirm your own balance is included.
At VIP 1 and above the maker fee is negative — you are paid for adding liquidity. The full schedule is published rather than negotiated privately.
About ninety-five percent offline in geographically separated vaults with multi-party signing; the rest sits in hot wallets sized for expected withdrawals.
Yes, mirroring production including the awkward error codes. Rate limits are documented per endpoint rather than discovered under load.

cta.title: Open an account
cta.sub: Verification usually completes within the hour, and the fee schedule is one page.

notes: A single yellow does all the brand voltage — CTAs, headlines, the mark and badges. Scarcely on dark, ubiquitously on transactional dialogs.
Numbers and prices use a separate face from body text so columns of figures align. That tabular consistency is non-negotiable in this system.
Marketing pages default dark and transactional pages flip light. Yellow CTAs and trading green/red are shared across both.
The homepage closes with a light footer beneath a dark body — a deliberate inversion that visually shuts the page.
Trading semantics are text colour only: green up, red down, never as badge backgrounds. Surfaces stay flat with no gradients.
